title: Battle Arena Pinball
author: jamaykdesign
selftext:
Hej hej!  
  
Battle Arena Pinball is an arcade game that started out as a cloudflare combat log experiment (warcraft logs/opendota style) that I was building for another project and eventually got fully eaten by Pinball :D

It was a MULTIPLAYER only game but on public request we implemented SOLO ranked with BOTS. And since we're big Marble League fans, a RACE mode was added too where you pick a BOT and watch it race in your name.   
  
You score in someone's post, you steal some land. Everything you score in your land is multiplied. 10 Waves, after each wave you choose a card, that's your build . 9 factions, you get extra points when playing 'at home'. Smash your friends and get a good leaderboard placement.   
  
For the multiplayer part, it's P2P private rooms and for public rooms I'm using cloudflare TURN relay server. I don't like it when big AAA games exposes your IP so all the public games go through a 3rd party service with a very small extra delay. Let's hope it won't be a smash hit (HAHA) because there's a lot of traffic on that server.

I'm a webdev/pm as a job, making games is just a side quest since we're all gamers in the house. I was AI assisted while coding this, but it's not fully vibe coded. I have spent countless of days redoing the rendering pipeline, budgeting every frame, canvas offloading, the custom combat log systems and more.

My wife is a VN BG artist, she helped with the art, style, colors and most of the props concepts that we tried to turn into procedural but we're not there yet. The Moles are done and we're very happy about it, all the other props need more love, we just need more time.

EVERYTHING AUDIO IS AI GENERATED! While it's been normalized in my industry to vibecode stuff and even required, I understand the artist debate. But I couldn't have done it w/o AI, not on my own and I also kinda like the results.

Another area where AI was doing heavy lifting: tests and balance. The more data I started to collect from each game, the easier it was for the AI to parse that data and help me balance things around, set the right numbers or rarity for the upgrades, even retire a couple of cards. While this is Season 1, we did have 2 small pre seasons and with the help of AI this one is as balanced as it's ever been. 

I used Claude Max 5X (Opus and Fable) for a lot of the coding and refactoring as the codebase grew. And Gemini PRO  (3.7 and 3.8 Flash) for the audio part.  
  
I've read stories on this sub about 1-shoting prompts into playable products but here it was more about iterating and playtesting; slowly discovering what this vertical slice could be while AIs being some very solid pair programming partners on my side.  
  
I hope you enjoy it, Cya on the leaderboards and thanks!  
  
And good luck to everyone else out there working on various passion projects!
